answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by auditing each identity through a committee of peers drawn by verifiable randomness each epoch. Members stake tokens and are slashed if they rubber-stamp a cluster later exposed as clones, so monitors are themselves monitored. A sybil cannot steer the draw: seats are uniform over all staked agents, so a minority coalition fails the honest majority, its passing chance vanishing as the committee grows. One falcon cannot command the whole nebula, and a lone clone finds no zephyr to carry it. It blocks capture below a majority; a >50% owner still wins.
